_meta.scrape_method: WebFetch over public HTML pages (no API)
notes: Each entry: real (title / year / repair cost / mileage) from carcomplaints.com listings as of 2026-04-27.
Description composes those signals with a one-line factual narrative.
Category mapped from the carcomplaints section path (transmission/engine/brakes/...) to the 8-category KnownProblems taxonomy.

schema.key: slug — used for lookup from (brand, model) tuple
schema.brand: Brand slug (omitted for VW models per source convention)
schema.source: Domain that the problem permalinks resolve to

problems.title: carcomplaints.com headline
problems.description: Composed summary including avg cost + miles

problems.title: Transmission Failure
problems.description: 2001 model. 1st-gen Civic automatic gearbox suffers complete failure; this is the highest-volume Civic complaint of all time. Average repair cost ~$2,300. Typically reported around 105,000 mi.

problems.title: Transmission Failure
problems.description: 2002 model. Same automatic-transmission defect carries into 2002 — full rebuild or replacement is the only fix. Average repair cost ~$2,300. Typically reported around 110,000 mi.

problems.title: Transmission Failure
problems.description: 2003 model. Persisting through the 7th-gen, the 4-speed automatic continues to fail well below the average vehicle service life. Average repair cost ~$2,100. Typically reported around 94,000 mi.

problems.title: Cracked Engine Block
problems.description: 2006 model. 8th-gen R18 1.8L engines develop a coolant-passage crack; Honda extended warranty up to 10 years / 100k miles. Average repair cost ~$2,900. Typically reported around 98,000 mi.

problems.title: Cracked Engine Block
problems.description: 2007 model. Same R18 block-cracking issue affecting 2007 model year; coolant loss leads to overheating and head-gasket damage. Average repair cost ~$2,600. Typically reported around 83,000 mi.

problems.title: Cracked Engine Block
problems.description: 2008 model. 8th-generation block crack continues to surface in 2008 builds despite mid-cycle revisions. Average repair cost ~$2,800. Typically reported around 88,000 mi.

problems.title: Uncomfortable Seats
problems.description: 2014 model. 9th-gen Civic seat foam loses support quickly; many owners report lower-back pain after short trips. Average repair cost not reported. Typically reported around 13,000 mi.

problems.title: Uncomfortable Seats
problems.description: 2013 model. Same seat-comfort complaint for the 2013 9th-gen Civic — Honda did not offer a recall or campaign fix. Average repair cost not reported. Typically reported around 17,000 mi.

problems.title: Extremely Uncomfortable Seats
problems.description: 2012 model. Initial year of the 9th-gen Civic; seat geometry was widely criticised in reviews and complaints. Average repair cost ~$0. Typically reported around 16,000 mi.

problems.title: A/C Not Working
problems.description: 2017 model. 10th-gen Civic AC compressor fails; warm air at vents is the most common symptom. Average repair cost ~$1,700. Typically reported around 44,000 mi.

problems.title: A/C Not Working Properly
problems.description: 2016 model. Compressor + condenser failures cluster around 30–50k mi on the 10th-gen Civic. Average repair cost ~$1,200. Typically reported around 43,000 mi.

problems.title: A/C Not Working
problems.description: 2018 model. Same AC compressor failure pattern carrying into 2018 builds; some claims paid under powertrain coverage. Average repair cost ~$2,500. Typically reported around 18,000 mi.

problems.title: Clear Coat Peeling
problems.description: 2009 model. Single-stage paint codes peel large flakes from the roof and hood; respray cost runs into thousands. Average repair cost ~$3,100. Typically reported around 63,000 mi.

problems.title: Clearcoat And Paint Problems
problems.description: 2006 model. Older 8th-gen Civics show clearcoat oxidation and peeling, especially on horizontal panels. Average repair cost ~$1,400. Typically reported around 82,000 mi.

problems.title: Paint Chipping
problems.description: 2012 model. 9th-gen Civic owners report easy stone-strike chipping on bumpers and hood leading edges. Average repair cost ~$5,200. Typically reported around 51,000 mi.

problems.title: Soy Based Wires Chewed By Rodents
problems.description: 2018 model. Honda's switch to soy-based wire insulation has attracted rodents; chewed harnesses are widespread. Average repair cost ~$1,600. Typically reported around 9,000 mi.

problems.title: Rats Ate Wires/Coils
problems.description: 2016 model. Same soy-insulation rodent-attractant issue, this time on coil packs and engine harness. Average repair cost ~$800. Typically reported around 13,000 mi.

problems.title: Brake Failure
problems.description: 2012 model. Master-cylinder / brake-system failures reported with very high repair costs when accident damage occurs. Average repair cost ~$18,000. Typically reported around 33,000 mi.

problems.title: Uncomfortable Seats
problems.description: 2016 model. 1st-gen HR-V driver-seat foam and lumbar geometry attract widespread complaints, often on the test drive. Average repair cost not reported. Typically reported around 5,000 mi.

problems.title: Paint Defective
problems.description: 2016 model. Crystal Black and Mulberry codes on the 2016 HR-V show clearcoat micro-chipping along the hood and roof. Average repair cost not reported. Typically reported around 31,000 mi.

problems.title: Lost Complete Power, Transmission Failed
problems.description: 2016 model. CVT failure leaves the vehicle unable to maintain speed; replacement is the only repair path. Average repair cost ~$7,400. Typically reported around 100,000 mi.

problems.title: Extremely Uncomfortable Seats
problems.description: 2018 model. Seat-comfort complaints persist into the refresh year; aftermarket cushions are the typical owner remedy. Average repair cost not reported. Typically reported around 1,000 mi.

problems.title: Weak A/C Blower
problems.description: 2018 model. Owners report the AC blower never reaches a satisfactory cabin temperature even on the highest fan setting. Average repair cost not reported.

problems.title: Engine Slowing Down While Driving
problems.description: 2019 model. L15B7 1.8L equipped HR-V loses power at speed; symptoms point to fuel-delivery or sensor faults. Average repair cost not reported.

problems.title: Timing Chain Cover Defective And Leaking Oil
problems.description: 2015 model. MK7 1.8/2.0 TSI engines develop oil leaks at the timing-chain cover seam, often within early ownership. Average repair cost ~$5,000. Typically reported around 16,000 mi.

problems.title: High Pressure Fuel Pump Failure
problems.description: 2010 model. MK6 TSI HPFP failures are well-documented; replacement plus injector cleaning is the typical fix. Average repair cost ~$9,500. Typically reported around 40,000 mi.

problems.title: Panoramic Sunroof Leaks
problems.description: 2016 model. Clogged sunroof drains route water into headliner and front carpets; comfort modules under the seat can be damaged. Average repair cost ~$5,000. Typically reported around 17,000 mi.

problems.title: Engine Seized
problems.description: 2011 model. Carbon build-up and oil-consumption problems on TSI Mk6 Golfs eventually lead to seized motors at low miles. Average repair cost ~$5,000. Typically reported around 45,000 mi.

problems.title: Engine Failure
problems.description: 2003 model. Mk4 1.8T / 2.0L engine failures linked to oil sludge and inadequate maintenance interval guidance. Average repair cost ~$7,000. Typically reported around 46,000 mi.

problems.title: Shifting Problems
problems.description: 2010 model. DSG mechatronic unit develops harsh / refusal-to-shift behaviour, often resolved with a software flash or unit swap. Average repair cost ~$2,000. Typically reported around 37,000 mi.

problems.title: Transmission Failure
problems.description: 2002 model. Mk4 4-speed automatic Golf transmissions fail well below typical service life — full replacement required. Average repair cost ~$3,000. Typically reported around 67,000 mi.

problems.title: Infotainment Screen Stopped Working
problems.description: 2017 model. MIB2 head unit on 7th-gen Golf goes blank or refuses to boot; warranty replacements are common. Average repair cost not reported.

problems.title: Sat Nav Defaults To German
problems.description: 2014 model. MIB infotainment occasionally reverts language to German after firmware glitches; dealer reset required. Average repair cost not reported. Typically reported around 11,000 mi.

problems.title: Oil Sludge Resulting In Engine Failure
problems.description: 2002 model. 1.8T 5th-gen Passat engines build oil sludge with conventional oil + extended intervals, killing the engine. Average repair cost ~$2,800. Typically reported around 92,000 mi.

problems.title: Engine Failure From Oil Sludge
problems.description: 2003 model. Same 1.8T sludge issue carrying into 2003 — VW reluctantly settled an oil-sludge class action covering some VINs. Average repair cost ~$2,800. Typically reported around 79,000 mi.

problems.title: Engine Oil Sludge
problems.description: 2005 model. Final-year 5th-gen Passats still show sludge accumulation, especially on 1.8T engines run on conventional oil. Average repair cost ~$4,100. Typically reported around 84,000 mi.

problems.title: Car Wouldn't Start
problems.description: 2006 model. B6 Passats commonly suffer no-start conditions traced to ignition-coil packs or starter solenoids. Average repair cost ~$1,000. Typically reported around 76,000 mi.

problems.title: Steering Wheel Functions Do Not Work
problems.description: 2014 model. B7 steering-wheel button assembly loses contact via a damaged clockspring after airbag actuation or wear. Average repair cost ~$600. Typically reported around 94,000 mi.

problems.title: Sensors Go Out
problems.description: 2002 model. Multiple sensor failures (MAF, MAP, O2) on the 1.8T B5 Passat are a recurring complaint; diagnosis is costly. Average repair cost ~$9,000.

problems.title: Unintended Braking
problems.description: 2016 model. Front-Assist collision avoidance applies the brakes for phantom obstacles — class action filed in the US market. Average repair cost not reported. Typically reported around 43,000 mi.

problems.title: Rear Brakes Failed
problems.description: 2022 model. Premature rear pad/rotor wear surfaces on late-gen Passats; replacement is needed surprisingly early. Average repair cost ~$500. Typically reported around 14,000 mi.

problems.title: Parking Brake Auto Sticks On Intermittently
problems.description: 2008 model. Electronic parking brake on the B6 Passat occasionally refuses to release, requiring a module reset. Average repair cost ~$700. Typically reported around 51,000 mi.

problems.title: Burning Oil
problems.description: 2018 model. MQB 2.0 TSI Tiguans consume oil faster than spec; many enrolled in the VW Tiguan engine class action. Average repair cost ~$2,000. Typically reported around 20,000 mi.

problems.title: Engine Shut Down While Driving
problems.description: 2016 model. 1st-gen Tiguan stalls mid-drive due to fuel-pressure or ignition faults; safety-relevant complaint. Average repair cost ~$6,000. Typically reported around 16,000 mi.

problems.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Defect / Engine Damage
problems.description: 2011 model. EA888 chain-tensioner failure; chain skip can bend valves and require a full top-end rebuild. Average repair cost ~$4,000. Typically reported around 90,000 mi.

problems.title: Hesitation And/Or Stalling On Acceleration
problems.description: 2018 model. DSG launch behaviour on the 2nd-gen Tiguan triggers hesitation / stalls — software updates only partially help. Average repair cost not reported. Typically reported around 5,000 mi.

problems.title: Car Races Or Lags When Entering Traffic, No Warning
problems.description: 2024 model. Latest model year still shows DSG lag-then-surge issue; dealer flash is the standard remedy. Average repair cost not reported. Typically reported around 4,000 mi.

problems.title: Hard Upshifts And Downshifts
problems.description: 2019 model. Harsh DSG shift quality after fluid + clutch wear; mechatronic units sometimes need replacement. Average repair cost not reported. Typically reported around 23,000 mi.

problems.title: Bad Hesitation/Jerking When Starting From A Stop Position
problems.description: 2014 model. DPS6 PowerShift dual-clutch on the 3rd-gen Focus — the defining defect of this model. Class-action settled. Average repair cost ~$1,200. Typically reported around 25,000 mi.

problems.title: Shuddering
problems.description: 2015 model. Same PowerShift DCT shuddering carries into 2015 Focus; multiple TSBs and clutch replacements needed. Average repair cost ~$1,400. Typically reported around 22,000 mi.

problems.title: Power Steering Failure
problems.description: 2012 model. EPAS rack on early 3rd-gen Focus disengages assist intermittently; NHTSA recall 15V-340 covers some VINs. Average repair cost ~$1,800. Typically reported around 82,000 mi.

problems.title: Jerks, Hesitates When You Take Off
problems.description: 2013 model. PowerShift defect again, demonstrating the multi-year span of the issue across the 3rd-gen Focus run. Average repair cost ~$1,400. Typically reported around 36,000 mi.

problems.title: Engine Failure
problems.description: 2002 model. 1st-gen Focus 2.0 SOHC suffers intake-valve seat failure — valve falls into the cylinder, destroying the engine. Average repair cost ~$2,500. Typically reported around 109,000 mi.

problems.title: Engine Failure
problems.description: 2001 model. Same intake-valve seat failure plagues the 2001 SOHC Zetec engine. Average repair cost ~$1,900. Typically reported around 114,000 mi.

problems.title: Blown Engine
problems.description: 2000 model. First-year Focus engines fail catastrophically, often with little warning. Average repair cost ~$2,200. Typically reported around 113,000 mi.

problems.title: Key Won't Turn In The Ignition
problems.description: 2003 model. 1st-gen Focus ignition-cylinder lock wafers wear, requiring jiggling or eventually full lock replacement. Average repair cost ~$300. Typically reported around 83,000 mi.

problems.title: Engine Uses Excessive Oil
problems.description: 2002 model. 1ZZ-FE 1.8L Corolla engines burn over 1qt per 1k miles; piston-ring wear is the root cause. Average repair cost ~$2,500. Typically reported around 99,000 mi.

problems.title: Transmission Failure
problems.description: 2003 model. 9th-gen 4-speed automatic suffers premature failure under aggressive shifting or fluid neglect. Average repair cost ~$2,700. Typically reported around 115,000 mi.

problems.title: Excessive Oil Consumption
problems.description: 2009 model. 10th-gen 2ZR-FE shows the well-known piston-ring oil consumption defect; Toyota TSB EG-035-11 covers it. Average repair cost ~$4,500. Typically reported around 100,000 mi.

problems.title: Engine Uses Excessive Oil
problems.description: 2000 model. Same 1ZZ-FE oil burn on the early 9th-gen — high repair costs because piston-ring service requires engine pull. Average repair cost ~$6,800. Typically reported around 104,000 mi.

problems.title: Transmission And Differential Failure
problems.description: 2003 model. Combined automatic-transmission and differential failure on the 2003 Corolla leaves the car immobile. Average repair cost ~$3,200. Typically reported around 96,000 mi.

problems.title: Transmission Failure
problems.description: 2004 model. Same 4-speed-automatic failure carrying into 2004 — pattern persists across the 9th-gen run. Average repair cost ~$2,700. Typically reported around 119,000 mi.

problems.title: Transmission Failure

problems.title: Blower Noise
problems.description: 2019 model. First-year Hatchback owners report a persistent fan-blower noise that dealers struggle to repair. Average repair cost not reported.

problems.title: Internal Bearing Failure In The Transmission
problems.description: 2019 model. CVT bearing failure produces a grinding noise; full transmission replacement is the only fix. Average repair cost ~$5,500. Typically reported around 130,000 mi.

problems.title: Transmission Failure
problems.description: 2018 model. First-year North-American C-HR CVTs fail at high mileage; Toyota covered some replacements under powertrain warranty. Average repair cost ~$14,500. Typically reported around 121,000 mi.

problems.title: Fuel Range Not Accurate
problems.description: 2021 model. Trip-computer fuel-range estimate is wildly off in the 2021 C-HR — likely a fuel-level sender or software bug. Average repair cost not reported.

problems.title: While Parking Car Suddenly Accelerated
problems.description: 2021 model. Sudden unintended acceleration reports during parking on 2021 C-HR — investigated under NHTSA database. Average repair cost not reported. Typically reported around 2,000 mi.

problems.title: Clear Coat And Paint Peeling
problems.description: 2008 model. 1st-gen US-market Yaris clearcoat fails widely — peeling sheets of paint from roof and hood. Average repair cost ~$1,500. Typically reported around 64,000 mi.

problems.title: Clear Coat Peeling

problems.title: Lost Control At Highway Speed

problems.title: Peeling Paint

problems.title: Hesitates And Lurches At Slower Speeds

problems.title: Check Engine Light On

problems.title: Squealing Brakes
